commits.headline: fix(workspace): per-field pre-load rail merge; backslash reopens a dismissed drawer
commits.body:
The per-Hub file has three fields, and each now carries its own pre-load
edited flag: showing or hiding the rail before the load keeps the
operator's visibility but still takes the file's panes and width, so the
write-back can no longer erase saved panes. A dismissed drawer (Esc) is
available but not on screen, so the first backslash brings it back
focused rather than hiding its retained state. Codex P2s on PR #105.

commits.headline: fix(tests): wait for the detail fixture to finish serving
commits.body:
IdlessOptionalEndpointEventsDeduplicateAcrossRefreshesWithoutServerCursors
asserted endpoint.Served.IsCompleted straight after the second fetch.
UnityWebRequest completes on the last Content-Length byte, which can land
before the fixture's thread-pool continuation disposes the client and
exits, so a busy full suite occasionally saw an unfinished task and
failed with a bare "Expected: True But was: False".

commits.headline: fix(workspace): pre-load rail edits keep panes and width apart
commits.body:
An explicit "rail width auto" before the per-Hub file loads was a no-op on
the initial 0, so the file's width won; and a width edit alone marked the
whole rail edited, which would have discarded the file's panes. Panes and
width now carry their own pre-load edited flags: the load takes only the
untouched parts from the file and writes back when anything was edited.
Codex P2 on PR #105.

commits.headline: fix(kernel): back off on infra failures instead of spending the retry budget (#1865)
commits.body: ## What / Why

commits.headline: fix(kernel): terminal CAS follows the cancelled orphan retry
commits.body:
Codex on #1865, round 8: cancelling the orphan retry attempt moves the
task's final-attempt pointer to it, so the terminal failed write's CAS on
the original attempt could never match and the task stayed running. The
terminal write now expects whichever attempt the task's pointer was left on.

commits.headline: fix(kernel): fail the task when the retry cannot return it to pending
commits.body:
Codex on #1865, round 7: if updateTaskStatus('pending') returned false after
the replacement attempt was created, the worker still announced the retry
and returned, leaving the task running with a finalized attempt and a queued
one nothing would claim. The transition result is now checked; on failure
the orphan attempt is leased and cancelled (best effort) and the task fails
on the terminal path with RETRY_TRANSITION_NOT_PERSISTED, the original
failure preserved.

commits.headline: fix(kernel): post-execution failures are fatal, and a retry that cannot be created fails the task
commits.body:
Codex on #1865, round 6. A failure after the agent ran was excluded from the
infra backoff but still matched the transient patterns (ETIMEDOUT from the
completion write), so the agent could be re-run anyway; post-execution
failures are now fatal for retry purposes. When createAttempt() throws after
the context already names the retry, the task used to stay running with no
attempt for anything to claim; it now fails on the terminal path with
RETRY_ATTEMPT_NOT_CREATED and the original failure pres

commits.headline: fix(kernel): only an explicit launch failure is pre-execution, and no probe outlives the grace
commits.body:
Codex on #1865, round 5. A returned `{ success: false }` means the agent ran
and reported the failure, whatever its text contains — a coding agent quoting
a repository panic or CLIENT_CLOSED must not be re-run — so every returned
failure is post-execution except the executor's explicit bridge preflight
failure (AGENT_BRIDGE_UNAVAILABLE). And a probe that starts exactly at the
grace deadline now gets at most 1 ms instead of its full timeout, while a
zero-deadline call keeps its single full probe.

commits.headline: fix(cli): correct the shadow-form test to match native association
commits.body:

form that lives inside the shadow root is unchanged.

commits.headline: fix(cli): accept a closed combobox that holds the requested value
commits.body:

commits.body:

commits.headline: fix(worker): report the queue position on a deduplicated dispatch too
commits.body:
Codex P2 on #1861: when idempotency reused a task that was still pending or
queued, delegate_task skipped the queue lookup and its response carried
neither `queue` nor the queue line, so a repeat caller learned nothing about
where the waiting task sat. The lookup now runs for any waiting task and the
deduplicated response carries the position and the line.

commits.headline: fix(cli): share the snapshot field cap across iframes
commits.body:
Parent and iframe forms draw from one budget of 120 fields, so a page of
frames cannot return a form list larger than the control cap.

commits.headline: fix(cli): accept a committed non-ASCII combobox value
commits.body:

commits.headline: fix(cli): do not bind a shadow field to a light-DOM form id
commits.body:

light-DOM form with the same id is not its owner.

commits.headline: fix(cli): compare select options and text writes exactly
commits.body:
Non-ASCII select values match the option text itself, and a longer
existing value no longer counts as the shorter write.

commits.headline: fix(kernel): never re-run an implementer whose finalizer failed
commits.body:
Codex on #1865, round 4: the babysit follow-on's own bridge preflight can
fail after the implementer has edited and committed the lane. The executor
returns that with a finalization stage and nonRetryable, but the worker threw
it before the post-execution stamp and the infra policy granted three more
whole runs. A returned result that names a finalization stage or is marked
non-retryable is now stamped post-execution, and planNextAttempt returns no
retry at all for a non-retryable result, whatev

commits.headline: fix(physics): objects resting on the desk ride along with pans and zooms
commits.body:
Roofs, chairs and citizens set down on the desk stayed fixed in the room
while the village slid under them. House walls swept into them and flung
them, and anything pushed far off the desk flew home and snapped on. Free
objects resting on the desk now move with the ground point under them,
keeping their height. Held, seated and travelling objects are unchanged,
and nothing is reparented.

commits.headline: fix(navigation): a flattening laser never whips the village
commits.body:
The laser drag followed the exact desk point under the laser. As the
laser flattens that point races away: about 17 cm per degree at 10°
from a hand 30 cm up, so pushing toward the far side or hand-tracking
wobble whipped the village at hyper speed. Steeper than 25° below level
the drag still follows the exact point. Flatter or rising lasers keep
moving at the gain the drag had at 25°, still capped at 1.5 m.

commits.headline: fix(agents): replay a pending question with everything the live event carried (#1862)
commits.body: ## What / Why

commits.headline: fix(cli): keep shadow labels and form-associated controls together
commits.body:
Shadow fields use their own tree for label[for], and a control with a
form attribute stays on that form instead of the orphan list.

commits.headline: fix(cli): keep label-chaos matches and honest combobox readback
commits.body:
A broken for= label and a whole-word name still match. Combobox success
requires the list to close or the option text to commit, and masked
text counts as stuck.

commits.headline: fix(agents): replay an external question with its structured questions and detail
commits.body:
Codex P2 on #1862: for a hook-observed AskUserQuestion, context.attention is
rewritten by every prompt, so its detail and questions are the current
prompt's data and the live event emits attention_detail, attention_questions
and question_count. The replay now treats attention.* as current for
external sessions (and permissions), carries the structured questions with
their count, and still keeps a plan's stale detail out of a hub-owned
question replay.

commits.headline: fix(kernel): keep returned launch failures pre-execution and bound each probe by the grace
commits.body:
Codex on #1865, round 3. The CLI executor returns its bridge preflight
failure as a resolved `{ success: false }` result that the worker rethrows
after executeAgent resolved, so the post-execution stamp landed on it and the
infra backoff never fired on the real path; the stamp now follows
classifyWorkerAgentResult(), which is where a returned failure is thrown, and
the policy also recognises the failure code carried on the result. And
waitForAgentApiBase() clamps each probe's timeout to the wait

commits.headline: fix(agents): keep a permission's own detail on replay
commits.body:
Codex P2 on #1862: for an external-session permission the hook path stores
the current command or path in context.attention.detail and creates no
pendingQuestion, so the previous gate dropped it on every replay. A
permission replay now falls back to attention.detail; a question replay
still takes only its own pending prompt or checkpoint detail, so a plan's
stale detail cannot ride along.

commits.headline: fix(cli): include shadow and iframe fields in snapshot forms
commits.body:
The forms list only walked the top document, so agents told to fill from
forms would miss the shadow and iframe fields the control list already shows.

commits.headline: fix(cli): fail autofill when a written field does not stick
commits.body:
autofill_profile uses the same fill expression as fill. success follows
result.failed so a miss is not reported as a completed profile write.

- o is the output-route key everywhere else, so it no longer doubles as

- Activity for a pane folded away behind a drilled view now accumulates
  as unseen instead of being cleared by the sidecar sync.
- The drawer (body under 98 columns) is drawn only while the rail has
  focus: a toggle focuses it, Esc puts it away with its panes intact, Tab
  brings it back, and a

commits.headline: fix(cli): fail fill when a field misses
commits.body:
Report unmatched keys and values that do not stick as success:false,
and score visible labels ahead of short name or id substrings.

commits.headline: fix(kernel): back off on the runtime that failed and never re-run a finished agent
commits.body:
Two Codex P1s on #1865. The infra backoff built its retry from the spec's
primary runtime, so a fallback attempt that hit a blip jumped back to the
primary that had already failed; the target now comes from the runtime the
failed attempt ran on (the attempt row records it). And a failure raised
after the agent finished — the completion write dying on CLIENT_CLOSED or a
query-engine panic — was classified as infra and scheduled up to three more
whole executions; the worker now stamps `error.stage

commits.body: ## What / Why

commits.headline: fix(agents): keep plan-era attention detail out of question replays
commits.body:
Codex P1 on #1862, second finding: context.attention.detail is written when
a plan is raised and is not cleared by a later ordinary prompt, so a question
or permission replay still carried the old plan markdown as attention_detail.
The replay now uses attention.detail (or the plan markdown) only on a plan
replay and otherwise takes the detail recorded by the current pending prompt
or checkpoint, if any.

commits.headline: fix(agents): log an ingest response that rejected the lifecycle event
commits.body:
Codex P1 on #1863: fetch resolves on a 401 (stale AGENT_INGEST_KEY) or a 500
from the ingest handler, so a rejected task_question / task_plan forwarded
from a platform process vanished without a trace. The client now checks
response.ok and logs the status and response detail through the same
non-fatal warning path a refused socket takes.

commits.headline: feat(workspace): keep u to remove the focused rail pane
commits.body:
A persisted agent task pin has no digit of its own, so u stays as the
one key that removes the focused rail pane (the pin picker and p are
still retired). Docs and the capture guide follow.

commits.headline: feat(workspace): chat-first navigation with rail pane toggles
commits.body:
Chat owns the body by default. The digits 2–6 no longer replace the
transcript with a destination; they toggle that destination's compact
pane in the rail beside chat (two stacked, a third replaces the oldest,
the key again removes it, the rail hides when the last pane goes). The
tab strip marks every rail pane with the pin glyph and brackets only the
drilled view. Enter or o on a focused rail pane drills into the full view,
which takes the whole body while the panes wait behind it; Esc or 1
ret

commits.headline: fix(agents): replay a plan body only when the pending prompt is a plan
commits.body:
Codex P1 on #1862: raiseQuestion() replaces lifecycle.execution.pendingQuestion
but leaves the approved plan in context.attention.plan, so a later ordinary
question replayed with the stale plan and its detail attached. The replay now
takes the plan body only when the stored kind is `plan` (or when nothing about
the kind is stored and the plan is the only evidence), reproducing the live
event instead of the history next to it.

commits.headline: fix(voice): treat intentional player recycles as cleanup, not route failures (#104)
commits.body:
The hub reports the last player exit's reason as routeFailure, so every
barge-in stamped interrupt_recycle on the session and voice health went
BLOCKED for good, hiding the RMS/VAD meters. The ingest now drops the
hub's intentional close reasons (interrupt, turn boundary and idle
recycles, backpressure timeout, device topology change, dispose) the way

commits.headline: fix(navigation): catch the laser over tall content near the desk edge
commits.body:
Village contents carry no rays, so a laser through the top of a house
near an edge used to pass it and meet the tabletop beyond the thin desk
slab, leaving no target. The laser now hovers on a math-only volume: the
desk footprint extruded to a little above the tallest roofline at the
current zoom. It has no collider, so the near grab and physics are
unchanged. A ray that starts inside the village misses, so letters and
panels keep priority and touch owns the inside.

commits.headline: fix(voice): classify the no-audio preferred-route retry kill as intentional
commits.body:
The recovery path kills the player on purpose before retrying the
preferred route; the retry's outcome, not the kill, reports a failure.
The UI-side intentional set now includes it so the retry cannot leave
routeFailure=no_audio_preferred_retry behind.

commits.headline: fix(respond): honor hub answerability and stop swallowing 409s (#415)
commits.body:
Approving a plan card on 2026-09-25 exposed two faults in the app's half of
the respond flow: every HTTP 409 from /respond was treated as "already
resolved", so a refused external_session_read_only silently dismissed the
card and left Mac-only copy behind; and Approve was offered in the card, the
push actions and the Live Activity regardless of the hub's can_respond.

commits.headline: fix(voice): stop reporting intentional player recycles as route failures
commits.body:
updateAudioState derived routeFailure from the last player exit's
intentional reason, but its intentional-reason filter only knew six UI
words while the jitter buffer's close reasons also include
interrupt_recycle, turn_boundary_recycle, idle_recycle,
backpressure_timeout and device_topology_change. A barge-in therefore
stamped routeFailure=interrupt_recycle, degraded the audio preference and
told the TUI the voice path was blocked for the rest of the session.
terminal-ui now consults the jitter

commits.headline: fix(voice): treat intentional player recycles as cleanup, not route failures
commits.body:
The hub reports the last player exit's reason as routeFailure, so every
barge-in stamped interrupt_recycle on the session and voice health went
BLOCKED for good, hiding the RMS/VAD meters. The ingest now drops the
hub's intentional close reasons (interrupt, turn boundary and idle
recycles, backpressure timeout, device topology change, dispose) the way
it already dropped route_change.

commits.body: Follow-up to #101, closes #102. commits.headline: fix(worker): report an unknown queue position when the lane lookup fails
commits.body:
Codex P2 on #1861: getRunningCliLanes() degrades to [] on a database error
because admission wants a best-effort answer, but getQueuePosition() read
that as "no lane is busy" and could tell a caller it was next up while every
lane was occupied. The lookup now has a throwing variant that the position
path uses inside its existing try, so a partial failure is the documented
`null` (unknown), and admission keeps its best-effort view.

(`--registration-timeout 600`; Claude Code's default when absent) and the
window is capped 30 s below it, inside the existing 30 s..15 min range. The
smoke asserts the flag mirrors the registration's JSON `timeo

commits.headline: fix(voice): claim Chatterbox children at spawn time, not at settle
commits.body:
The bounded shutdown wait narrowed the leak but could not close it: a cold
start slower than the cap still exits with a live Python child, and neither a
latch nor a kill-on-timeout can help, because after process.exit() no code
runs and settle-time ownership has no handle to kill before then.

commits.headline: fix(voice): keep the shutdown wait timer ref'd
commits.body:
An unref'd deadline timer lets Node exit naturally while the shutdown wait is
still awaiting a pending warm, skipping the stop the wait exists to reach and
turning a failed shutdown's exit 1 into a natural 0. The timer is always
cleared and the only caller exits immediately after, so unref bought nothing.

commits.headline: fix(voice): wait for a pending lazy warm before Chatterbox teardown
commits.body:
A lazy Chatterbox warm spawns its Python child long before it settles, and
the handle only reaches start-voice-server's ownership variable from the
warmer's settle handlers. Shutdown stopped whatever it already held and then
called process.exit in the same tick, so a warm still pending at teardown
stranded a serving child holding the GPU and its port.

commits.body:
Codex P1 on #400: NSPredicate's MATCHES operator isn't supported against
the SQLite store, so the previous fix could make every
requiresUserAttentionPredicate() fetch throw instead of filter (Inbox,
Sidebar, watch snapshot). Revert the predicate to its SQLite-safe exact
"!= ''" form and close the whitespace-only gap at the actual entry point
instead: RemoteTask's attentionType decode now normalizes (trim,
blank-to-nil) via the same firstNonEmpty helper already used for
attentionMessage/resultSum

commits.headline: fix(tasks): reject whitespace-only attentionType in predicate too
commits.body:
Codex review on #400: hasUnresolvedAttention trims via nilIfEmpty, so a
whitespace-only attentionType (e.g. "  \n\t ") is treated as unset. The
predicate's exact "!= ''" check missed that case. Switch to a MATCHES
check against the whole-string whitespace pattern so both "" and any
all-whitespace value are rejected, matching the property. Extends the
regression test with a whitespace-only case.

commits.headline: fix(tasks): align requiresUserAttentionPredicate with requiresUserAttention
commits.body:
Task.requiresUserAttentionPredicate() disagreed with the requiresUserAttention
property on two edges: a nil status (the property treats it as .pending via
the taskStatus fallback, the predicate excluded it entirely) and an
empty-string attentionType (the property's hasUnresolvedAttention uses
nilIfEmpty and treats it as unset, the predicate counted it as set). Fixes #398.

disappeared, breaching this PR's own Review Contract ("a following
keyword

previous turn (e.g. agent-intent's `agents`, which exposes the delegation

The conditional native tools of a granted group (agent-intent's `agents`
group carries the delegation tools) were loaded from the persisted group
list the caller read before the turn. With the persist no longer awaited,
a follow-up arriving while the previous turn's write was in flight loaded
a list without that group and lost the tools, the same staleness the
pattern set was just protected against.

commits.headline: fix(tools): the resolved-profile pass extends this turn's sticky batch (#1586)
commits.body:
applyStickyIntentGrants replaced the conversation's sticky batch size on
every call, so the resolved-profile pass, a second call in the same turn,
shrank the batch to its own few patterns and resolveEagerGrantWindow fell
back to the policy window on the follow-up; the request-time batch's
older patterns flipped to defer_loading. With `extendBatch` the second
pass adds to the turn's batch, and the next turn's request-time pass
starts a new one.

commits.body:
The caller loads runtime_tool_state before the turn and the request
re-seeded it into the in-memory grant set every time, refreshing each
entry's LRU position. With the persist no longer awaited, that snapshot
can lag a write still in flight, so the re-seed moved stale entries ahead
of the pattern the previous turn had just granted and evicted it at the
cap; the keyword-free follow-up then lost the tool.

commits.body:
_prioritizeTools orders the grant tier by position in the bypass list
(newest last) when the pool exceeds the cap. The workflow's required tools
came first, so a conversation with enough accumulated grants ranked them
oldest and cut them before optional sticky tools. composeBypassPatterns
puts them last of all, after this turn's intent patterns.

again on the follow-up, flipping their defer_loading bytes in the tools
prefix on exactly the turn that should be stable.

inference to persist an optimization. The call is no longer awaited: the
in-memory grant set is what this process serves from, the row only
matters to a later process.

commits.body:

rotated which grants carried defer_loading and flipped prefix bytes on a

(external and advisor tools merged, byte-stable order, defer_loading set)
and is keyed by type, name and deferral, emitted once per request and
diffed against the conversation's previous request. A re-match of
already-granted intent patterns no longer refreshes their LRU position,
so the eager window and its deferral bytes stay put.

Two request_tool_group calls in the same round were each priced
against that round's bare prompt_tokens, so grant B ignored grant A's
tokens and both could look like they fit the same headroom. Add a
turn-scoped accumulator that resets when the loop reports a new

commits.headline: fix(voice): refuse a zero served count and key the grant cache by schema (#1569)
commits.body:
A served count.input_tokens that is identical with and without `tools`
means the server ignored the tool defs, not that the group costs
nothing. Math.max(0, ...) turned that into a free grant, which can push
an over-budget group past oMLX's window. Return null (uncached) instead
so the caller falls back to the conservative estimate.

commits.headline: docs(voice): describe localRuntimeToolGrants without the removed cap
commits.body:
The comment above `localRuntimeToolGrants` still described the 24-tool count
cap removed by the grant-budget work (#1569, #1568), contradicting the code.
It now describes the current contract: server-qualified tool identities
granted this session, appended monotonically and never evicted so the tools
block only grows and the prefix cache survives, bounded by the token budget
onToolGroupRequest prices per grant rather than by count.

commits.headline: fix(voice): price tool-group grants against oMLX's window, persist whole grants (#1569, #1568)
commits.body:
A request_tool_group grant is now priced with the served tokenizer (estimate
when the server does not answer) against the window oMLX enforces, minus a
reserve and the round's prompt_tokens. A group that does not fit is refused
with a message that says what to ask for instead; an accepted group persists
every usable tool, so the next turn's tools block matches this turn's last
round. The 24-tool count cap is gone: the budget bounds growth in the unit
oMLX enforces.

commits.headline: fix(voice): make resolveMlxModel() engine-aware, not just mlx-launcher's own default

scripts/realtime-mcp-agent.js actually calls and passes straight into
ensureMlxServer() as an explicit `model` — bypassing mlx-launcher.js's
own DEFAULT_MODEL fallback entirely, since that fallback only fires
when the caller supplies no `model` option at all. Round 1 fixed
mlx-launcher.js's *unreached* default; this fixes the real caller.

commits.headline: fix(agents): treat an lsof read with warnings as unverifiable in the broker-only check
commits.body:
lsof -t silences warnings, so a lane directory lsof could not read hid
the processes inside it and the partial pid list could still pass as
broker-only. The lane read now passes +w, and lsofOutput returns null
whenever stderr carries anything. Exit 1 alone stays normal: under +D
lsof exits 1 whenever any listed file is not open.

commits.headline: fix(autojack): harden route audit migrations
fix(agents): re-check broker idleness inside the reap, right before SIGTERM
commits.body:
A client that connected after cleanupOrphans' idle check was still
signalled, because reapCodexBrokers re-listed processes and sent SIGTERM
without looking at the sockets again. The reaper now takes a requireIdle
guard, runs it immediately before signalling, and returns every broker
as a survivor when it fails. cleanup() passes no guard, so the reap on
removal from #1652 is unchanged.

commits.headline: Let the escalation probe pin sampling seeds
commits.body:
With --seed N, every request in a prompt's turn carries a sampling seed:
one per prompt and repetition, shared by both arms and recorded on each
record. oMLX honors it, and the same request with the same seed generates
the same output from a cold prefill or a cached one, so two sweeps with
the same N pair turn by turn. A reworded prompt can then be compared
against the original on the same random draws instead of across runs whose
rates swing on their own (#1626).

commits.headline: Let the escalation probe repeat chosen prompts
commits.body:
--only <id,...> runs just those corpus prompts, in corpus order, and
--repeat N runs them N times, arm A then arm B per repetition. Both
require --part prompts; an unknown id exits 1 before any model call.
A repeated sweep numbers each record and error with `rep`, and the
per-prompt summary keeps one row per repetition. A single sweep's
records and summary are unchanged.

commits.headline: fix(trials): drop the checkout key that could lock out an eligible retry (#133)
commits.body:
An account-scoped idempotency key on the trial Checkout create is the only
thing covering Stripe finishing server-side after IN_FLIGHT_MS, because it
makes an aborted POST and its retry one operation. It cannot be made to
work: the body under it carries the request origin, the source, and
metadata[claim_token], and the token changes with every claim by design, so
Stripe refuses the reuse and an eligible account retrying from a different
CTA is locked out until the key is pruned, up to 24 hours.

commits.body:
Both 409s in createTrialCheckout fire after the claim is won and before
attachTrialSession runs, so a bare throw left a session-less claim that
reads as in-flight and 409s an eligible account for two minutes. A refused
key with nothing to recover now releases the claim; a replayed complete
session attaches its id, because that trial really was spent.

commits.headline: fix(trials): make trial checkout creation idempotent per account
commits.body:
An aborted Checkout POST that Stripe is still processing has produced no
listable session yet, so the claim-token recovery finds nothing, releases
the claim, and lets a second trial out behind the first. Key the create on
the account so the retry is the same operation. A refused key is itself the
signal that a trial checkout exists: recover it or 409, never create a
second. A replayed session that is complete is a spent trial; one that is
expired gets a fresh session under the claim's own key.

commits.headline: fix(billing): say plainly when a subscription has been cancelled
commits.body:
Cancelling from the Stripe portal is cancel-at-period-end by default, so Stripe
leaves the status alone: a trialing subscriber who cancels stays `trialing`
until the period closes. Every field this dashboard stored was therefore
identical before and after, and the screen someone returned to from Stripe was
the screen they left. There was no way to tell whether it had worked.

went mid-air every time. Reject sub-minimum hits inside the loop instead,
so the surface behind them is still found.

Every coloured element in the instrument is a LineRenderer or a
ParticleSystem, and both carry colour only as mesh vertex colour.
All of them shared a material built from URP/Unlit, which declares

resolved white at full alpha. The cyan/violet/magenta palette was
computed each frame and thrown away, and because alpha was pinned
to 1 every fade in the system was inert as well.

oMLX/dflash-mlx reuses a cached snapshot only when that snapshot's ENTIRE
token sequence is a prefix of the incoming request
(dflash_mlx/cache/prefix_l1.py: `if req_tuple[:snap_len] != snap.token_ids`),
and snapshots are stored at full length — prompt AND generation. A hit
therefore requires turn N+1 to continue turn N verbatim.

ambiguity on a real challenge.

commits.headline: fix(voice): release PvRecorder before fatal checkpoint persist
commits.body:
unhandledRejection/uncaughtException waited up to 5s on recovery
checkpoint I/O before teardown. Watchdog SIGKILL is 1s, so that await
could strand the HAL client. Release the recorder as soon as the crash
is classified fatal.

commits.headline: fix(voice): do not open a PvRecorder after shutdown starts
commits.body:
SIGTERM during initializeWakeWord() used to leave recorder null, so
early teardown was a no-op; main() then constructed a mic while
finalizeProcessExit() was still in jitter-buffer/DB awaits. Gate
initializeMicrophone() and the main() call site on shutdownInProgress,
and release if construct raced the flag.

commits.headline: fix(voice): release PvRecorder before long shutdown awaits
commits.body:
Watchdog SIGKILL is 1s; jitter-buffer dispose alone can take 6s.
finalizeProcessExit() now drops the HAL input client first so a
watchdog restart cannot kill the process with the recorder still live.

commits.headline: fix(voice): do not mint a PvRecorder after shutdown starts
commits.body:
A shutdown-induced read() failure was treated as device loss and could
construct a replacement mic after cleanupVoiceResources() had already
run. Reacquire now bails on shutdownInProgress and releases any
in-flight replacement before commit.

commits.headline: fix(voice): release PvRecorder on fatal startup exits
commits.body:
initializeMicrophone() can leave a live recorder before a later startup
step throws. The main() catch now tears it down so watchdog restarts
cannot strand that HAL client either.

commits.headline: fix(voice): release PvRecorder on agent shutdown
commits.body:
stop() only pauses capture; release() drops the CoreAudio HAL input
client. Shutdown and failed reacquire now share teardownPvRecorder()
so watchdog restarts cannot strand coreaudiod clients.

The hard-gate quiescence check ran once at the top of main() and was reused
as a stale snapshot for the entire 15-25 minute serialized sweep. A voice
turn or Chatterbox generation starting after the sweep began (this workflow
is enabled: true, so this runs unattended nightly) went undetected for the
rest of the run, defeating the gate's whole purpose — being in the way is
the one cost no measurement is worth (quiescence.js's own doc comment).

commits.headline: fix(voice): give request_tool_group its real schema in gauntlet toolset
commits.body:
toolDef() had no canonical entry for request_tool_group, so it fell through
to the generic unknown-tool fallback ({ arg: string }). usedEscapeHatch()
(predicates.js) scores a call against { request: ... } instead — a model
faithfully following the ONLY schema it was ever shown could never satisfy
the predicate, so the escape shape false-failed regardless of capability.
This is the root cause behind the 0/1 escape baseline tracked in #1392.

commits.headline: fix(test): tolerate Prettier-wrapped app.use() in memory-config-route test

The mount assertion matched a single line containing both `app.use(` and
the route path. That line is 86 chars — over this repo's printWidth:80 —
so Prettier wraps it across multiple lines once the file is reformatted,
which is exactly what merging origin/main into this stack's tip does. The
route was never misconfigured; the test's line-based matcher just could
not see it split.

commits.body:
Codex review: pressing s or w before the workspace has received its
first frame tick or envelope recorded an arm time of zero, because
workspaceDisplayTime() is zero until then. The next tick sets the clock
to a real timestamp, so the computed age became the whole span since the
epoch and the three-second window expired instantly. During startup, and
throughout --no-runtime, a user who armed before the first tick could
only ever re-arm — the confirm was unreachable.

palette while typing mode stayed active. The palette was not in the
modal pre-empt, so the next key edited the hidden composer while a
visible palette sat frozen, and esc exited typing rather than closing
it.

whole graph by 30 ticks. `merge` now returns a `MergeOutcome` reporting
the nodes and edges IT added, and `apply` uses that.

commits.headline: feat(sync): serve the signed catalog to enrolled devices
commits.body:

autoworks-ai/autovault on feat/https-sync-upstream, so this matches that wire
contract rather than proposing one: `autovault link <slug>` resolves to

commits.body:

Cloud slugs expand to https://autovault.dev/v/<slug>/catalog.json
(override with AUTOVAULT_CLOUD_ORIGIN). On a TTY, wait for owner admit;
--json and non-TTY return pending immediately.

commits.headline: feat(sync): enroll HTTPS signed catalogs
commits.body:
Add a transport for AutoVault Cloud catalogs over HTTPS without changing
the signed-release domain. Devices POST a public key, land pending, and
install only after signature, bundle hash, and per-file SHA-256 checks.
Bundle URLs are pinned to bundles/<bundle_hash>.json relative to
catalog.json. Beta: rotating the publishing key forces re-enrollment.

commits.headline: fix(trial-g): the backdrop was blurred and lit by a compression it never had
commits.body:
w describes how compressed the BAND is. A backdrop pixel's lookup relaxes
toward the plain mapping regardless of w -- that is the whole point of the
squash -- but the mip level and the brightness boost right after the sample
were still derived from w on its own. So a genuinely undistorted backdrop
sample got blurred and brightened as if it were as compressed as the band
beside it, and worse the deeper the descent ran, since w only ever shrinks.

commits.headline: fix(trial-g): the padded mesh was still in the radius, corner or vertex
commits.body:

not eliminate the padded-bounds problem, because one mesh in the art tree IS its
padding. TrialAMeshBuilder.BuildParticles displaces its vertices in-shader for
orbit motion and overrides mesh.bounds afterward to compensate -- the explicit
2.5-unit cubic bound is correct for that mesh's actual on-screen extent, not
excess to trim. Reading its corners reported ~2.165 units against a 1.08-unit
rim; reading its true verti

`classifyToolName('delegate_task')` returned `'other'`, and the action-claim guard
matches `classifyToolName(entry.name) === claimClass` — so a **successful** delegation

confirmation usually names one, so `runLocalNativeToolLoop`'s guard (#1549) reached
`outcome: 'gave_up'` and blanked the turn's `finalText`: a correct delegation the user
hears as silence.

3. The workflow validates and is scheduled after the loopback smoke.

prs.title: feat(voice): two-tier quiescence gate (7/11 gauntlet)
prs.body:
## Review Contract
1. Presence, a recent voice turn, or Chatterbox generating → never run.
2. Load above the ceiling → abort; merely loaded → run with latency withheld.
3. All aborts are `skipped`, never `fail`. Probes fail closed.

prs.title: feat(voice): deterministic scoring and regression detection (6/11 gauntlet)
prs.body: Built on `src/voice/eval/` rather than beside it — the probe DSL and the gate-vs-advisory → fail/weak/pass rule already exist and are what the voice eval suites speak. A second grader would drift within a month.

prs.title: feat(voice): two execution planes with one output shape (5/11 gauntlet)
prs.body: `model` hits `/v1` directly at temperature 0; `runtime` drives the REAL `runLocalNativeToolLoop` with the production persona, allowlist and sampling. Both return identical keys so a predicate cannot tell them apart.

prs.title: feat(voice): shape grammar deriving ground truth from structure (4/11 gauntlet)
prs.body: A generated challenge has no ground truth. Asking a model "what would be hard for you?" produces prompts nobody can score, and inherits the generator's blind spots — it cannot invent a test for a weakness it does not know it has.

prs.title: feat(voice): canonical synthetic toolset + export the real allowlist (3/11 gauntlet)
prs.body: `tool-ladder.mjs`, `local-fast-bakeoff.js` and `local-tools-smoke.js` each define `get_weather` with a different parameter name (`city` vs `location`), so "the same toolset" meant three incompatible things. This is the single source for new code; the three older harnesses keep their own defs until retired, so their measured baselines cannot shift underneath them.

prs.title: feat(voice): round-aware scoring predicates (2/11 gauntlet)
prs.body: The scoring vocabulary a shape-derived challenge is checked with. Lifted from `scripts/tool-ladder.mjs`, plus two new predicates: `fanIn` (an action that must follow every lookup) and `usedEscapeHatch` (request the group, then use the grant).

prs.title: fix(voice): ladder budget-exhausted round + wire AG-UI suite into CI (1/11 gauntlet)
prs.body: First of a stacked series (1/11) adding the **local gauntlet** — a loop that generates escalating tool challenges for the local voice model, scores them deterministically, and trends them against a committed baseline. This PR is the foundation: two real bug fixes plus a preserved measured record. It stands alone and is useful without the rest.
